draft.rationale: Concept Mapping fits this novice study session because the goal is to retrieve the sequence and link it to where glycolysis happens, then repair only what the attempt exposes. The session stays bounded to the two current targets and uses one unsupported first attempt before a concise map, evidence check, and repair.

coverage.focus: Retrieve and connect the order of the main stages of cellular respiration and the location of glycolysis.
essentialIdeas: Glycolysis comes first in cellular respiration
The Krebs cycle comes after glycolysis and before the electron transport chain
completionEvidence: Attempt each target without notes and correct any exposed gap

evidenceMap.essentialIdea: Glycolysis comes first in cellular respiration
The Krebs cycle comes after glycolysis and before the electron transport chain

deferredContent: Glycolysis does not require the mitochondrion

methodBriefing.name: Concept Mapping
methodBriefing.what: You will first answer from memory, then name the connections between the stages, then check whether your answer matches the target evidence, and finally repair any gap.
methodBriefing.why: This fits a novice conceptual-learning task because the goal is not just recall but showing the order as linked relationships, then fixing the exact missing link.
how: Answer the first question without notes.
Build the connection between the named stages with clear relationship phrases.
Check the answer against the target evidence.
If a gap appears, correct only that gap and try again.
methodBriefing.completion: The session is complete after every required activity is attempted and the exposed gap is corrected in the final repair step.
personalization: YOVA is using the current task and session objective as the starting point until your completed work provides more evidence.

activities.label: Try
activities.title: Stage order from memory
activities.body: Without notes, name the three main stages of cellular respiration in order.
activities.correctAnswer: Glycolysis first, then the Krebs cycle, then the electron transport chain.
activities.feedback: Check the order only. This is a closed-note retrieval step, so the answer should name the stages in sequence.

activities.label: Connect
activities.title: Map the stage links
activities.body: Connect the three stage names with relationship phrases.

methodRuntime.instructions: Connect the named concepts with relationship phrases.

connections.expectedRelationship: The Krebs cycle comes after glycolysis.

connections.prompt: What comes after the Krebs cycle?
connections.expectedRelationship: The electron transport chain comes after the Krebs cycle.

activities.correctAnswer: The Krebs cycle comes after glycolysis. The electron transport chain comes after the Krebs cycle.
activities.feedback: The map should show a true sequence, not just three separate labels. Use relationship words like first and after.

activities.label: Check
activities.title: Match the evidence
activities.body: Which statement is the best evidence that glycolysis happens in the cytoplasm?
choices: Glycolysis happens only in the nucleus.
Glycolysis happens in the cell membrane.
Glycolysis happens inside the mitochondrion matrix.
activities.feedback: The location claim is about where glycolysis occurs in the cell. Cytoplasm is correct because glycolysis takes place there, outside the mitochondrion.

activities.label: Repair
activities.title: Fix the gap
activities.body: If your answer missed glycolysis location, correct it now in one sentence.
activities.feedback: Repair only the missed location. The target fact is the cell location, so the correction should name the cytoplasm directly.
